excerpt: This appendix contains detailed definitions for each Capability Threshold in Section 2.
paraphrase: The appendix provides detailed definitions of each Capability Threshold referenced in Section 2.

context_stem: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons:
excerpt: CBRN-3: The ability to significantly assist individuals or groups with basic STEM backgrounds in obtaining, producing, or deploying CBRN weapons.
paraphrase: CBRN-3 is the capability to significantly help STEM-background actors obtain, produce, or deploy CBRN weapons.

excerpt: We assess this by comparing what potential attackers could achieve with full model access versus 2023-level online resources, assuming they have funding and up to one year of time to invest, but no initial specialized expertise.
paraphrase: Assessment compares model-assisted attacker capability against 2023-level online resources, assuming funding and up to one year, but no prior specialized expertise.

context_stem: Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) weapons:
excerpt: CBRN-4: The ability to substantially uplift CBRN development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs (with relevant expert teams), such as by novel weapons design, substantially accelerating existing processes, or dramatic reduction in technical barriers.
paraphrase: CBRN-4 is the ability to substantially advance state-level CBRN programs via novel design, acceleration, or barrier reduction.

excerpt: We currently define this as uplifting a team of people with skills equivalent to entry-level PhD biologists to be able to approximate the capabilities of a world-class, state-backed bioweapons team.
paraphrase: CBRN-4 is currently defined as uplifting entry-level PhD-equivalent biologists to approximate world-class state-backed bioweapons team capability.
stated_bar: entry-level PhD biologists to world-class state-backed bioweapons team

excerpt: AI R&D-4: The ability to fully automate the work of an entry-level, remote-only Researcher at Anthropic.
paraphrase: AI R&D-4 is the ability to fully automate an entry-level, remote-only Anthropic researcher's work.

excerpt: AI R&D-5: The ability to cause dramatic acceleration in the rate of effective scaling. Specifically, this would be the case if we observed or projected an increase in the effective training compute of the world's most capable model that, over the course of a year, was equivalent to two years of the average rate of progress during the period of early 2018 to early 2024.
paraphrase: AI R&D-5 is the ability to dramatically accelerate scaling, defined as achieving in one year an increase equivalent to two years of the 2018-2024 average progress rate.

excerpt: We roughly estimate that the 2018-2024 average scaleup was around 35x per year, so this would imply an actual or projected one-year scaleup of 352 = ~1000x.
paraphrase: The estimated 35x/year average scaleup implies AI R&D-5 corresponds to a roughly 1000x one-year scaleup.

excerpt: Model Autonomy checkpoint: The ability to perform a wide range of advanced software engineering tasks autonomously that could be precursors to full autonomous replication or automated AI R&D, and that would take a domain expert human 2-8 hours to complete.
paraphrase: The Model Autonomy checkpoint is autonomous performance of advanced software engineering tasks taking a human expert 2-8 hours, as precursors to fuller autonomy.

excerpt: We primarily view this level of model autonomy as a checkpoint on the way to managing the risks of robust, fully autonomous systems with capabilities that might include (a) automating and greatly accelerating research and development in AI development (b) generating their own revenue and using it to run copies of themselves in large-scale, hard-to-shut-down operations.
paraphrase: This autonomy level is viewed as an intermediate checkpoint toward managing risks from fully autonomous systems capable of accelerating AI R&D or self-funding replication.

excerpt: We are uncertain how to choose a specific threshold, but we maintain a current list of specific CBRN capabilities of concern for which we would implement stronger mitigations.
paraphrase: Anthropic maintains a list of specific concerning CBRN capabilities warranting stronger mitigations, despite uncertainty on precise thresholds.

excerpt: We treat these lists as sensitive, but we plan to share them with organizations such as AI Safety Institutes and the Frontier Model Forum, and keep these lists updated.
paraphrase: These sensitive lists will be shared with bodies like AI Safety Institutes and the Frontier Model Forum and kept updated.

excerpt: This comparison is hard to make in practice; this note is to clarify the meaning of the conceptual threshold and the fact that this policy aims to measure risk relative to the world in 2023, so that we can understand how much risk the current generations of frontier models are creating.
paraphrase: This footnote clarifies that the comparison is difficult in practice, and the policy intends to measure risk relative to a 2023 baseline.

excerpt: The 35x/year scaleup estimate is based on assuming the rate of increase in compute being used to train frontier models from ~2018 to May 2024 is 4.2 x/year (reference), the impact of increased (LLM) algorithmic efficiency is roughly equivalent to a further 2.8 x/year (reference), and the impact of post training enhancements is a further 3 x/year (informal estimate).
paraphrase: The 35x/year estimate derives from combining 4.2x/year compute growth, 2.8x/year algorithmic efficiency gains, and 3x/year post-training enhancement gains.

excerpt: Combined, these have an effective rate of scaling of 35 x/year.
paraphrase: The combined effective scaling rate from all three factors is 35x per year.
